    Diagonal quadratic forms #

    This file provides general infrastructure for diagonal quadratic forms expressed as weighted sums of squares.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.equivalent_weightedSumSquares_comp: reindexing the coefficients preserves equivalence.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.equivalent_weightedSumSquares_of_pair: a binary equivalence extends across fixed coordinates.
    • QuadraticMap.associated_weightedSumSquares, QuadraticForm.toMatrix'_weightedSumSquares, and QuadraticForm.discr'_weightedSumSquares: over a ring in which two is invertible, the associated bilinear form of a diagonal form is the weighted dot product, its Gram matrix in the standard basis is the diagonal matrix of the weights, and its discriminant is their product.
    • QuadraticMap.nondegenerate_weightedSumSquares: over a ring in which two is invertible, a diagonal form with regular weights is nondegenerate.
    • QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares_units: unit weights may be replaced by the scalars they name.
    • QuadraticMap.neg_weightedSumSquares: negating a diagonal form negates its weights.
    • QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares_apply_three_single and QuadraticMap.not_anisotropic_weightedSumSquares_of_ternary_eq_zero: evaluating a diagonal form on a linear combination of three distinct basis vectors, and deducing that a ternary solution with a nonzero third coordinate gives a nonzero isotropic vector.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.isSquare_prod_mul_prod_of_equivalent: isometric diagonal forms with unit weights have weight products differing by a square.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.equivalent_weightedSumSquares_of_pair {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} {i j : ι} [CommSemiring R] [Fintype ι] {w w' : ι → R} (hij : i ≠ j) (hpair : (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R ![w i, w j]).Equivalent (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R ![w' i, w' j])) (hrest : ∀ (k : ι), k ≠ i → k ≠ j → w k = w' k) :
    (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R w).Equivalent (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R w')

    Replacing two distinct coefficients by an equivalent binary form, while fixing all other coefficients, produces an equivalent diagonal form.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.equivalent_weightedSumSquares_comp {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} {κ : Type w} [CommSemiring R] [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (w : ι → R) (σ : κ ≃ ι) :
    (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R w).Equivalent (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R (w ∘ ⇑σ))

    Reindexing the coefficients of a diagonal form does not change its equivalence class.

    source
    theorem QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares_units {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} [CommSemiring R] [Fintype ι] (w : ι → Rˣ) :
    weightedSumSquares R w = weightedSumSquares R fun (i : ι) => ↑(w i)

    A diagonal form with unit weights is the diagonal form with the underlying scalar weights.

    source
    @[simp]
    theorem QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares_apply_three_single {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} [CommSemiring R] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (a : ι → R) {i j k : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) (hik : i ≠ k) (hjk : j ≠ k) (x y z : R) :
    (weightedSumSquares R a) (Pi.single i x + Pi.single j y + Pi.single k z) = a i * x ^ 2 + a j * y ^ 2 + a k * z ^ 2

    Evaluate a diagonal form on a linear combination of three distinct coordinate vectors.

    source
    theorem QuadraticMap.not_anisotropic_weightedSumSquares_of_ternary_eq_zero {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} [CommSemiring R] [Fintype ι] (a : ι → R) {i j k : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) (hik : i ≠ k) (hjk : j ≠ k) {x y z : R} (hz : z ≠ 0) (h : a i * x ^ 2 + a j * y ^ 2 + a k * z ^ 2 = 0) :
    ¬(weightedSumSquares R a).Anisotropic

    A ternary solution with a nonzero third coordinate gives a nonzero isotropic vector in a diagonal quadratic form.

    source
    theorem QuadraticMap.neg_weightedSumSquares {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} [CommRing R] [Fintype ι] {S : Type u_1} [Ring S] [Module S R] [SMulCommClass S R R] (w : ι → S) :
    -weightedSumSquares R w = weightedSumSquares R (-w)

    Negating a weighted sum of squares negates its weights.

    source
    @[simp]
    theorem QuadraticMap.associated_weightedSumSquares {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} [CommRing R] [Invertible 2] [Fintype ι] (w x y : ι → R) :
    ((associated (weightedSumSquares R w)) x) y = ∑ i : ι, w i * (x i * y i)

    The bilinear form associated with a diagonal quadratic form pairs the coordinates diagonally: it is the weighted dot product.

    source
    @[simp]
    theorem QuadraticForm.toMatrix'_weightedSumSquares {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} [CommRing R] [Invertible 2] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (w : ι → R) :
    toMatrix' (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R w) = Matrix.diagonal w

    The matrix of a diagonal quadratic form in the standard basis is the diagonal matrix of its weights.

    source
    @[simp]
    theorem QuadraticForm.discr'_weightedSumSquares {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} [CommRing R] [Invertible 2] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (w : ι → R) :
    discr' (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R w) = ∏ i : ι, w i

    The discriminant of a diagonal quadratic form is the product of its weights.

    source
    theorem QuadraticMap.nondegenerate_weightedSumSquares {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} [CommRing R] [Invertible 2] [Fintype ι] {w : ι → R} (hw : ∀ (i : ι), IsRegular (w i)) :
    Nondegenerate

    A diagonal form with regular weights is nondegenerate when two is invertible. Over a domain the hypothesis is that every weight is nonzero (isRegular_iff_ne_zero).

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.isSquare_prod_mul_prod_of_equivalent {R : Type u} {ι : Type v} {κ : Type w} [CommRing R] [Invertible 2] [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] {w : ι → Rˣ} {v : κ → Rˣ} (h : (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R w).Equivalent (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares R v)) :
    IsSquare ((∏ i : ι, w i) * ∏ i : κ, v i)

    Isometric diagonal forms with unit weights have weight products differing by a square. An isometry of the coordinate spaces changes the Gram matrix of a diagonal form by a congruence, so it changes its determinant — the product of the weights — by the square of the determinant of that isometry.
